title: Preventing Feedback Loops in a Two-Way Vue Unit Converter
summary:
If both fields in a Vue unit converter are editable, how do you stop a calculated result from overwriting the user's input? I use explicit conversion directions and synchronous watchers so that each numeric edit updates the opposite field without bouncing back.

A Vue length converter gave me a compact example. Each side can update the other, both results are rounded, and a swap button changes units and values together. The arithmetic is routine; the interesting part is stopping intermediate state from becoming a new user instruction.

One Conversion Function, Two Directions

The component imports a shared length-unit table and conversion helper. Each unit has a scale relative to meters, so a conversion goes from the source unit to meters and then from meters to the destination unit.

title: Vercel Sandbox starts up to 4x faster
summary:
Vercel Sandbox now initializes up to 4x faster outside the Washington, D.C. (iad1) region when reused image data is served from a regional cache.

Initialization now reads cached image data close to where the sandbox runs, avoiding round trips to origin image storage in iad1 on cache hits. Regional caching supports managed and custom images backed by Vercel Container Registry, including snapshots based on those images.

In internal end-to-end benchmarks with Vercel Managed Images, startup time fell about 75% in Paris and from about 3.5s to 1.05s in Seoul. Regions closer to origin storage generally see smaller improvements because requests already travel a shorter distance.

Learn more in the Vercel Sandbox documentation.

title: Google Cloud Moves the Compute Engine API to Immutable Date-Based Versions
summary:
Google Cloud has made date-based versioning of the Compute Engine API generally available, replacing the single mutable /v1 surface with immutable quarterly snapshots such as 2026-09-01, selected per request with a header or query parameter. New versions can change defaults, error formats, and IAM checks without touching /v1 callers, a model Azure Resource Manager and Stripe have used for years.

title: Bus factor 1 is the default: per-language ownership in 195 popular repos
summary:

  • Bus factor is the fewest people who together made 80% of a file's commits; a bus factor of 1 means one person made 80% or more of them.
  • In the median of 195 popular open-source repos (1,000+ GitHub stars), 60% of production files have a bus factor of 1, and in 124 of the 195 those files are the majority.
  • Busy files are more shared: in the median repo, 25% of hotspot files have a bus factor of 1.
  • Numbers come from repowise's index of those 195 repos (November 2026), plus a git shortlog script run on a full clone of Django.

Bus factor (also called truck factor) is the number of people who would have to disappear before nobody left understands a piece of code. A bus factor of 1 means one person holds it.

title: UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713: how to check your server and apply the hot-patch
summary:
In short: if you run UnrealIRCd 6.0.0 to 6.2.7 (or version 5), your server is affected. Version 6.2.7.1, released on 7 November 2026, fixes it, and a hot-patch does the job without a restart. The vendor reports attack attempts, and the US agency CISA added CVE-2026-114713 to its catalog of exploited vulnerabilities on 13 November (deadline for federal agencies: 16 November).

What is the problem?

The implementation of the IRCv3 label tag does not escape characters properly when it echoes the tag into replies. An ordinary user can therefore inject newlines and other characters into the traffic between linked servers. The injected commands run with the authority of the server, for example KILL or GLINE. The maintainer found the flaw himself in an internal audit done with the help of AI.
